hook: $40 an hour looks fine. You need $74.65
hook_say: $40 an hour looks fine. But if clients pay for 60% of your hours, a $60,000 take-home needs $74.65.

rows.label: Take-home pay you want
rows.say: You want to take home $60,000 a year
rows.why: The calculator's example goal: $60,000 a year after tax and costs.

rows.label: Tax set-aside + yearly costs
rows.say: Add $26,000 for tax and business costs
rows.why: A 25% tax set-aside on the take-home is $20,000, plus $6,000 of yearly business costs.

rows.label: Money you must bring in
rows.why: $60,000 plus $20,000 of tax set-aside plus $6,000 of costs.

rows.label: Hours clients pay for (60%)
rows.say: Clients pay for 1,152 of your 1,920 hours
rows.why: 48 weeks of 40 hours is 1,920. Clients pay for 60%; the rest is admin, quotes and travel.

rows.label: What $40 an hour brings in
rows.why: 1,152 paid hours at $40. That is $39,920 under the $86,000 you need.

rows.label: Hourly rate you need
rows.why: $86,000 spread over 1,152 paid hours is $74.65 an hour.

fix.label: Rate needed if clients pay for 70%
fix.say: Get clients to pay for 70% of your hours and you need $63.99
fix.why: Same goal, tax and costs over 1,344 paid hours: $63.99 an hour. The calculator shows 50, 60, 70 and 80% side by side.
